Editor's restoration with uncertainty mark (+); ⲁⲥⲉ visible. ⲛϩ̄ as conjunctive 'and (one) shall' fits — ⲛϩⲁⲥⲉ possibly 'and shall make/multiply.' Could alternatively read ⲍⲁⲥⲉ 'many' or related. Confidence low.
ⲉϩⲃⲣⲁ visible, ⲓ̈ⲧ restored; ⲉϩⲃⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲧ qualitative — likely cognate with ⲛⲉⲧⲃⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲧ 'the radiant ones' in glossary, here in singular 'a radiant man.'
Single letter ⲍ restored at start of line 24; ⲛ̄ visible. Lyc. ⲍⲛ̄ = ϩⲛ̄ 'in.'

notes.decision: Chapter heading: 'the Dragon, the one of the foremost (rank) of the head.' In standard Manichaean cosmology the Dragon is the belly of the King of Darkness (cf. accumulated entry ⲡⲇⲣⲁⲕⲱⲛ 'belly of King of Darkness IS dragon'). The phrase ⲡⲁⲧⲙⲛⲧⲉϩⲧⲉ ⲛⲁⲡⲉ 'the one of foremost rank of the head' may indicate either (a) a topological reorganization of the body-schema specific to this kephalaion, or (b) ⲛⲁⲡⲉ functions adverbially 'at the top/foremost' independently of the body-mapping. Translation preserves the ambiguity.

notes.coptic_form: [ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ ⲁ] ⲟⲩⲉ ⲍⲛ ⲛⲉϩⲙⲁⲑⲏⲧⲏⲥ ϣⲛ ⲡⲁⲡⲟⲥⲧⲟⲗⲟⲥ
notes.decision: Editor's restorations follow the standard Kephalaia chapter-opening formula attested throughout the corpus. ϣⲛ = Lycopolitan reflex of ϣⲓⲛⲉ 'ask, inquire.'

Translated 'fore-rank of head.' The accumulated glossary registers ⲙⲛⲧⲉϩⲧⲉ as an abstract from ⲉϩⲧⲉ/ϩⲏⲧ ('front, before') = 'the foremost, front rank.' In this kephalaion the phrase functions in apparent equivalence to ⲧⲥⲁϣϩⲃⲉ ⲛ̄ⲁⲡⲉ 'seven-fold of head' (line 25), suggesting the Magousaeans' dragon was envisaged as having multiple heads at the front. 'Fore-rank of head' preserves the abstract genitive structure while signaling the multi-headed sense.

Lexeme not securely identifiable. Possible analyses: (a) Lyc. reflex of ϣⲱϣϥ̄ 'destroy, scatter,' giving plural 'scatterings/dispersals'; (b) related to ⲥⲁϣϥ̄ 'seven' through metathesis/orthographic variation, giving 'in five sevens' = thirty-five; (c) a designation of the dragon's coils or limbs. Left transliterated; flagged in proposed_terms.

Translated 'thou shouldst expound forth' — 2sg conjunctive of an extended causative on ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲥ 'raise, declare.' Cf. parallel form ⲧⲛⲁⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲉⲧⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in L15 ('I shall expound to thee'), where the -ⲉⲧⲕ marks 2sg.m dative. Here the -ⲉⲧ ending without explicit suffix is unusual; possibly a frozen verbal extension or an unmarked dative. Captures the act of complete revelation/exposition.

Translated 'which they have uttered in a virginity.' ⲧⲉⲟⲩⲁϩ likely related to causative on ⲟⲩⲱϩ 'add/place upon' or to ⲧⲁⲩⲟ 'utter, send forth' in extended form. ⲙⲛⲧⲡⲁⲣⲑⲉⲛⲟⲥ 'virginity/maidenhood' here functions either as 'in figurative/hidden form' (a saying spoken of/under the figure of a Virgin) or with reference to the Manichaean cosmic Virgin of Light. The reading is preserved literally with the directional sense of utterance plus a quasi-allegorical specification.

'The seven sense-organs' — ⲁⲓⲥⲑⲏⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ is Greek αἰσθητήριον. The seven enumerated below are: 2 eyes (ⲡⲙⲁⲛⲓ̈ⲱⲣⲍ̄ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ), 2 ears (ⲡⲙⲁⲛⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ), 2 nostrils (ⲡⲙⲁⲛϣⲱⲗⲙⲉ ⲥⲛⲉⲩ), and 1 tongue (ⲡⲕⲉⲗⲉⲥ) — totaling seven. The Apostle's pneumatic decoding of the Magousaean seven-headed dragon: the 'seven heads' ARE the seven sense-organs of the human head. Direct correspondence in the strict Manichaean sense: not metaphor, but identity at the spiritual register.

'And the tongue' / 'the also-tongue' — ⲡⲕⲉ- ('the other / the also') + ⲗⲉⲥ ('tongue,' Lyc. for ⲗⲁⲥ). The seventh sense-organ in the head's enumeration: where eyes/ears/nostrils each come in pairs (= 6), the tongue is single, completing the seven. ⲕⲉⲗⲉⲥ functions to mark the additional/concluding seventh.

Translated 'the foremost-bust of the man' — Greek προτομή 'bust, foremost portion (of the body).' Cf. accumulated glossary entry ⲡⲡⲣⲟⲧⲟⲙⲏ as Manichaean technical title 'Protomē/Foremost-Image' for the Third Ambassador; here used naturalistically of the upper portion of the human body where the seven head-senses are situated, paired antithetically with ⲡⲥⲁⲛ̄ⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'the lower side' (L27).

Translated 'act as foremost-of-head' preserving the compound idiom: ⲣ̄- (do/act as) + ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲉϩⲧⲉ ('foremost rank,' cf. glossary) + ⲛ̄ⲁⲡⲉ ('of head'). The cosmological sense: heaven and the lower regions are perfected and become 'the foremost head' over the dragon (= enthumesis). Direct correspondential identification.

Lycopolitan reflex of Greek δράκων 'dragon' (cf. ⲡⲇⲣⲁⲕⲱⲛ in glossary as 'belly-dragon of King of Darkness'). The dragon here is identified explicitly in line 11 with τ enthumesis of the body. Five caves = five members/parts of the dragon-as-enthumesis.

Translated tentatively 'throat' — body-part filling the second slot in the dragon's five caves (after tongue, before heart). Etymology uncertain: possibly Lyc. for a throat/gullet term, or related to ⲡⲟⲩⲁϥ 'fleshy organ' in glossary. Confidence low; awaits parallels.

Translated tentatively 'breath' — fourth member of the dragon's body-parts (after heart, before the bond). Etymology unclear; possibly related to ⲛⲓϥⲉ 'breathe' or a Lyc. lexeme for lung/respiration. Confidence low.

Translated 'who is the enthumesis': feminine relative pronoun ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲥ ⲧⲉ agrees with feminine predicate ⲧⲉⲛⲑⲩⲙⲏⲥⲓⲥ even though formal antecedent ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲕⲱⲛ is masculine — standard Coptic predicate-attraction. The dragon IS the enthumesis (correspondential identification, not comparison).

Translated 'prevail over her': ⲃⲣⲟ here = ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ/ϫⲣⲟ 'prevail, conquer' (cf. ⲡⲃⲣⲟ in glossary as both 'joy/triumph' tentative and 'prize'). The pair ⲥⲱⲭⲉ ('fight') + ⲃⲣⲟ ('prevail') + ⲍⲱⲧⲃⲉ ('slay') forms a victory sequence over the enthumesis-dragon.

Translated 'the prize': substantival ⲃⲣⲟ in line 15 means 'the victory/prize received' — the eschatological reward for conquering the dragon. Same root as the verb in line 12 ('prevail'); here as noun. Cf. ⲃⲣⲟ tentative 'joy/triumph' in glossary.

Translated 'the days of his going-forth': ⲃⲓⲛⲉⲓ as Lyc. nominalization on ⲃⲓ/ⲃⲱⲕ 'go' (or related); 'his going-forth' = his exit/departure (likely euphemism for death). The phrase modifies ⲍⲓⲥⲉ 'toil': 'with no toil of the days of his exit.' Confidence moderate.

Translated tentatively 'I am intent for' as a 1sg form of attention/blessing toward those who slay the dragon. Possible analyses: (a) Lyc. ⲛⲉⲓ-ⲉⲧⲱⲣϩ̄ '(I) am watchful/attentive'; (b) ⲛⲉⲓ-ⲱⲡ 'I reckon (blessed)'; (c) some 1sg blessing-formula. The disciple expresses eager attention/benediction for those who slay the enthumesis-dragon. Confidence low.

Translated 'kill him' as Lyc. 3sg.m suffixed form of ⲙⲟⲩⲟⲩⲧ 'slay, kill,' paralleling and reinforcing ⲍⲁⲧⲃⲉϩ 'slay him' (= ϩⲱⲧⲃ̄). The doublet 'kill him and slay him' intensifies the act of conquering the dragon.
